name: Beat a friend
summary: Wins the run the moment score passes a friend's score; the HUD shows "Beat <friend>: <score>".
when_to_use: Friend challenges: "beat my score". Pair with score and a lose path (lives, timer_bar or countdown); leave score's own target at 0.
api: requires state score:int; the app passes friend_name and target; emits target_beaten once when score > target

name: Checkpoint
summary: Saves the best progress seen so far at safe moments and hands back a restore value (minus a penalty) after a setback, so a slip does not reset the whole run.
when_to_use: Longer runs where losing everything on one mistake would feel harsh: platform stages, wave survival, distance runs.
api: game provides function progress_now() -> int and emits checkpoint_reached; bind setback to life_lost or any event; game applies restore_checkpoint {value} itself; provides state checkpoint

name: Branching story
summary: Scenes of up to four short lines with 2 or 3 choice buttons; each choice leads to another scene, and scenes can be good or bad endings (up to 60 scenes).
when_to_use: Story, mystery and choice games; any game where reading and picking a path is the play. Track clues or trust with game state on choice_made.
api: game declares state story_lines (4 per scene), story_labels (3 per scene), story_next (3 per scene, scene numbers as strings), story_ends (1 per scene: '', 'good', 'bad'), usually from content; provides state scene and input choose; optional scene and button sprites

name: Collision check
summary: Circle overlap between the player and a list of points the game owns; emits hit with a grace window, plus particles, shake and haptic.
when_to_use: Any dodge, catch-the-bad-thing or obstacle game. Feed it spawns from spawn_wave or the game's own objects; bind lives to hit.
api: requires state player:vec2 and function colliders() -> list<vec2>; provides hit_at, safe_until; the game removes the hit object in its own rule on hit

name: Combo multiplier
summary: A streak counter: each good hit raises combo up to a max, a bad hit resets it; combo_mult (1 + combo) multiplies points.
when_to_use: Rhythm, tapping, catching and quiz games where a streak of good moves should pay more.
api: game emits hit_good and hit_bad; provides combo, best_combo, combo_mult; emits combo_broken

name: Countdown clock
summary: A visible clock that counts down and emits time_up at zero, optionally winning or losing the game; it warns in the last seconds.
when_to_use: Timed runs: score attack, survive until the clock ends, beat a puzzle before time runs out.
api: emits time_up; on_end none | win | lose; does not set the game's time_limit

name: Daily seed
summary: Marks a run as the day's shared puzzle. The host passes the day's seed (same for everyone in a Group) so everyone gets the same game; shows "Daily · <day>".
when_to_use: Daily puzzles and Group daily sets where everyone plays the same board and compares.
api: host starts the game with the day's seed and passes day_label; provides state daily:bool; emits nothing

name: Difficulty curve
summary: One float knob, difficulty, that ramps from a start to an end value over a set time with a chosen easing, then holds.
when_to_use: Any action game that should get harder smoothly; read difficulty in spawn gaps, speeds or sizes.
api: provides state difficulty:float; curve linear | ease_in | ease_out | ease_in_out

params.curve: enum, linear | ease_in | ease_out | ease_in_out, default "linear"

name: Endless levels
summary: No win condition; a level counter climbs every few seconds and emits level_up so the game can raise difficulty.
when_to_use: Endless runners, survival and score-attack games. Needs its own lose path (lives, timer_bar).
api: provides state level; emits level_up; sets no objectives; leave time_limit unset

name: Fuzzy answer match
summary: Pure functions that decide whether typed text matches an accepted answer: ignore case, accents, punctuation, a leading article, word order, plurals and number words; forgive typos by length (4 letters or fewer exact, 5-7 one typo, longer at threshold); optional phonetic match. Deterministic.
when_to_use: Custom typed-answer rules (with a text input: the iPhone keyboard): names, titles, spells, open answers. typed_answer already uses it, so do not add it there.
api: fuzzy_ok(input, entry) -> bool; fuzzy_best(input, entries: list<string>) -> int (-1 if none); fuzzy_score(input, name) -> float 0..1; fuzzy_passes(input, name, score) -> bool; fuzzy_entry(input, entry) -> float; fuzzy_key(s) -> string (normalized). An entry is an answer plus aliases joined by =, e.g. "hermione granger=hermione". Spec: authoring/SPEC.md 2.12

name: Friend ghost
summary: Races a friend's recorded run: a ghost score rises from 0 to the friend's final score over their run time, shown next to yours.
when_to_use: Async friend challenges where you watch yourself pull ahead of or fall behind a friend in real time. Pair with beat_target for the win.
api: requires state score:int; the app passes friend_name, friend_score and friend_time; provides state ghost; emits passed_ghost and ghost_passed_you once each

name: Tap to jump
summary: Tap to hop against gravity onto a floor, with an optional double jump; provides the player position and draws the floor and avatar.
when_to_use: One-button jumpers and side runners: jump over obstacles, hop for pickups. Conflicts with player_drag and lanes.
api: provides state player:vec2 (fixed x) and vel_y; emits jumped and landed; optional avatar and ground sprites

params.tone: enum, primary | secondary | accent | ink | danger, default "primary"

name: Tap grid
summary: A tappable board of square cells (2 to 10 per side) that sends tap_cell; the game paints each cell's colour and label. It has no rules of its own.
when_to_use: Board, grid and tile games: match pairs, tic-tac-toe-like boards, pixel picking, minesweeper-like reveals, grid logic puzzles.
api: game provides functions cell_fill(c: ivec2) -> string (hex or '') and cell_label(c) -> string; sends input tap_cell {cell}; cell index = c.y * cols + c.x; optional cell sprite

name: Hint button
summary: A limited-use hint button: each tap spends a hint and turns hint_active on for a short cooldown.
when_to_use: Puzzles and memory games where a few helps keep players from getting stuck; the game decides what hint_active reveals.
api: provides state hints_left and hint_active; emits hint_used

name: On-screen keyboard
summary: A grid of drawn on-screen keys, one per character of a letters string; tapping sends press {letter}. Keys colour by the game's key_state.
when_to_use: Only when the keys themselves are the game: Wordle-style letter grids with per-key colours (word_check), letter tiles to spell from (hives, wheels, hangman), crossword and cryptogram cells, typing-speed games where key positions matter. NOT for typing an answer, a name, a number or a question: those use the iPhone keyboard (typed_answer, qa_bank, or a text input).
api: game provides function key_state(letter) -> int (0 untouched, 1 good, 2 bad), unless word_check provides it; sends input press {letter}; cols * rows >= letters

name: Lane switching
summary: Moves the avatar one lane left or right (3 to 5 lanes) on a tap of either half of the screen; draws lane strips and the avatar.
when_to_use: Lane runners and dodgers: switch lanes to avoid what comes down or grab pickups. Conflicts with player_drag and gravity_jump.
api: provides state player:vec2, lane:int and function lane_x(i) -> float; emits lane_changed

params.tone: enum, primary | secondary | accent | ink | danger, default "primary"

name: Lives
summary: N lives; each hit costs one and the game is lost at zero. Shows "Lives: N" or a row of life sprites.
when_to_use: Any game with mistakes that should end the run after a few: dodgers, quizzes (bind hit to answered_wrong), memory games.
api: requires event hit (bind it to collide's hit or any wrong-move event); provides state lives; emits life_lost

name: Memory match
summary: Face-down cards in pairs on a grid_board; flip two at a time, matches stay up, misses flip back; matching every pair wins.
when_to_use: Memory and matching games, with themed card faces per symbol.
api: listens to grid_board's tap_cell (cols must equal the board's); provides state cards (symbol, revealed, matched), selected, matches; emits pair_found and pair_missed; optional card sprite

name: Pickups
summary: Collectibles that appear in place, fall from the top or scroll in from the right; touching one with the player collects it and emits point.
when_to_use: Catch and collect games, runners with coins, and any game with things to grab.
api: requires state player:vec2 and event point (from score or the game); provides state items and collected; emits collected_one; optional pickup sprite

name: Play the clip
summary: Hear a clip, then pick an answer: plays the game's melody clip for each quiz question shortly after it appears and draws a Play again button (limited replays, not while playing) above the question.
when_to_use: Any listen-then-answer quiz with melody_clip content: guess the decade, which instrument, name the jingle. Pair with quiz (clip i = question i, in content order), rounds, score and lives. Give quiz a time_ms of at least (replays + 1) x clip_ms + delay_ms + 3000.
api: requires quiz (state order, qi, locked; event question_done); game writes sound.clips; sends input replay_clip; provides clip_now, replays_left, current_clip(); emits clip_play {clip}

params.clips: int, default 4, 1..12 (the number of clips; question indexes wrap)
params.label: string, default "Play again", max 14 chars

name: Drag to steer
summary: Drag to move an avatar along x, y or both, snapping to the finger or gliding toward it; draws the avatar.
when_to_use: Dodgers, catchers, paddles and shooters where the player steers directly. Conflicts with gravity_jump and lanes.
api: provides state player:vec2; axis x | y | xy; mode follow | glide; optional avatar sprite

params.tone: enum, primary | secondary | accent | ink | danger, default "primary"

name: Multiple-choice quiz
summary: Multiple-choice questions (2 to 4 choices) one at a time with a draining time bar; shows the right answer after each pick.
when_to_use: Trivia and knowledge quizzes where picking from choices is right. For typed or open answers use typed_answer instead.
api: game provides functions quiz_questions(), quiz_choices() (choices per question, flattened) and quiz_answers() (exact correct text), all list<string>; provides question_text, correct_answer, right_count, wrong_count; bind rounds' round_done to question_done and score's point to answered_right; quiz_questions() may read `locked` to show an explanation during the reveal (give reveal_ms 2500+); quiz_questions() may read `locked` to show an explanation during the reveal (give reveal_ms 2500+)

params.reveal_ms: duration, default 700, 300..8000 (longer when quiz_questions() shows notes while locked)
params.cols: int, default 1, 1..2 (2 columns for short answers, leaving room for a picture)

name: Progress reveal
summary: Hidden text that uncovers letter by letter as a progress number rises; can win when fully revealed.
when_to_use: A message, title or secret that the player earns by playing: a birthday note, a puzzle answer, a story line.
api: requires state reveal_progress:int (bind to score or another rising int); provides reveal_text and revealed; emits fully_revealed

params.text: string, default "Something good is coming", max 80 chars

name: Rounds
summary: A finite run of N rounds; counts round_done events and wins after the last round.
when_to_use: Quizzes, typed answers and any game played as a fixed set of rounds or questions.
api: requires event round_done; provides state round; emits round_started {index} and all_rounds_done

name: Score
summary: A score that rises on each point event, with an optional target that wins.
when_to_use: Almost every game with points. Not with typed_answer, which keeps its own score.
api: provides state score and event point; games may also write score directly

name: Sequence memory
summary: Watch-and-repeat pattern memory on 3 to 6 coloured pads; each success adds one more step, a wrong tap replays the pattern.
when_to_use: Memory and rhythm-flavoured games where players repeat a growing sequence.
api: sends input pad {index}; provides pattern, pos, showing, lit, best_len; emits sequence_ok, sequence_wrong and pad_ok; optional pad sprite

name: Group progress
summary: A Group's combined total across everyone's runs: this run's score adds to what the Group already has, toward a shared goal with a progress bar.
when_to_use: Cooperative Group challenges: everyone's runs fill one shared goal.
api: requires state score:int; the app or backend passes group_name, group_total and goal; provides group_progress; emits goal_reached once

params.group_name: string, default "Hill Street Crew", max 20 chars

name: Sort into bins
summary: One item name at a time; tap which of 2 to 4 labelled bins it belongs in, against a per-item timer.
when_to_use: Sorting and categorising games: this-or-that, sort the snacks, which house would they be in.
api: game provides functions bin_items(b) -> list<string> and bin_label(b) -> string; sends input choose {bin}; provides deck, item_i, right_count, wrong_count, verdict and current_name(); emits sorted_right and sorted_wrong

name: Spawner
summary: Spawns round objects from one edge at a steady rate and moves them straight across, removing them when they leave.
when_to_use: Hazards, enemies or items that stream across the screen: dodgers, catchers, simple shooters. Pair with collide and speed_ramp.
api: provides state spawns and spawn_speed; emits spawned; from top | bottom | left | right; optional hazard sprite

params.from: enum, top | bottom | left | right, default "top"

name: Speed ramp
summary: Raises spawn_speed by a step every few seconds, up to a maximum.
when_to_use: Any spawner game that should speed up over time.
api: requires state spawn_speed (from spawn_wave)

name: Sliding merge board
summary: A 3x3 to 6x6 board where each swipe slides every tile and merges equal neighbours into double value; a new tile appears after each move.
when_to_use: Merge puzzles in the slide-and-combine genre, with themed tiles per value.
api: sends input slide {dir} from swipes or arrow keys; provides state board and functions best_tile(), can_move(board), merge_line; emits slid, spawn_tile, merged {value}; loses when no move is left; optional tile sprite

name: Draining timer bar
summary: A time bar that drains every tick and refills on a refill event; empty either loses or just emits time_out.
when_to_use: Fast games where good moves buy more time: keep-it-going tapping, rapid sorting, speed rounds.
api: requires event refill; provides state time_left and drain_mult; emits time_out; on_empty lose | emit_only

name: Pass and play
summary: Pass-and-play for 2 to 4 people on one phone: each takes turns in rotation behind a "Pass to <name>" overlay, with running totals.
when_to_use: Party and couch games where friends share one phone and compare scores.
api: game emits turn_done {points}; provides turn_player, turn_active, turn_totals, turn_no and turn_name(i); emits turn_started and all_turns_done; run play rules only while turn_active

name: Typed answer
summary: Open-answer prompts the player answers by typing on the iPhone keyboard (a native text field over the answer box; Return submits); answers (with aliases joined by =) are matched forgivingly by the fuzzy_match rules and score by rarity tier (common to legendary), with a per-prompt timer.
when_to_use: Typed trivia and naming games ("name a…", fill-in, guess the word, rarest-answer trivia): anywhere multiple choice would be wrong.
api: brings its own text field (do not add keyboard); game provides ta_prompts() and ta_answers() (tiers split by |, answers by ,, aliases by =), both list<string>; provides prompt_text, ta_progress, ta_candidates (bot answers), ta_points, typed, last_result, last_answer; inputs ta_enter (Return) and ta_edit (each edit); emits answered_right {points, tier}, answered_wrong, prompt_done; matching ignores case, accents, punctuation, articles, word order, plurals and number words and forgives typos by length (threshold, phonetic params); not with quiz or score; keep the bottom 45% of the screen calm (the iPhone keyboard covers it)

params.placeholder: string, default "Type your answer", max 30 chars

notes: conflicts with quiz, score; version 2 (native text field); version 1 used the keyboard grid (authoring/tools/convert-native-keyboard.mjs moves old games over)

name: Waves
summary: Escalating waves with a break between; a wave ends when its enemies are cleared or after a set time; clearing enough waves wins.
when_to_use: Wave survival, tower defense and shooter games with breathers between rounds.
api: provides state wave and in_break; emits wave_started {index}, wave_cleared, all_waves_cleared; the game emits enemies_gone in clear mode

name: Word guess check
summary: Guess a hidden word with per-letter feedback (right place, in the word, absent) over a limited number of guesses.
when_to_use: Hidden-word guessing games with letter feedback, themed word lists, daily words.
api: requires state answer (lowercase, exactly length letters) and keyboard's press input; provides key_state(letter), letter_mark(guess, c), guesses, typed, solved; emits word_solved, guess_wrong; emit word_reset to start a new word

name: Ask yes/no questions
summary: The player types free yes/no questions about a mystery on the iPhone keyboard and presses Return; a deterministic matcher maps each question to one of the case's pre-written facts (written by Muse at build time) and answers Yes, No, Doesn't matter or Partly, showing which question it answered. Key facts are clues; after tapping Solve, Return checks a typed theory against the solutions. Unmatched questions get "Ask another way" and cost nothing.
when_to_use: Lateral-thinking and situation puzzles, twenty questions about a hidden thing, interrogating a suspect or witness, "ask the oracle" games: anywhere the player asks in their own words and a fixed answer is enough. Not for free conversation or judging creative text (use npc_judge with written replies).
api: brings its own text field (do not add keyboard); game provides qa_setups(), qa_reveals(), qa_facts(), qa_solves(), all list<string> one entry per case, from the qa_bank_content step (qa-bank/1, authoring/expander/qa-bank.mjs toContent): fact strings "<y|n|i|p>[*]|<question shown>|<group>|<group>", words in a group joined by =, facts by ;; provides case_text(), questions_left(), reply_label(r), qa_progress(), qa_candidates() (bot questions), state typed, solving, asked, clues, solved_count, qa_points, last_reply, last_ask, history, locked, revealing, ran_out; inputs qa_enter (Return), qa_edit, and the Ask and Solve mode buttons qa_ask, qa_solve; not with typed_answer, quiz or score

params.question_points: int, default 25, 0..1000 (per question left on a solve)
params.goal: int, default 1, 0..20 (cases solved to win; 0 never wins on its own)
params.placeholder: string, default "Ask a yes or no question", max 30 chars

gaps_it_closes: free-typed questions answered without an LLM at play time
notes: matching is authoring/expander/intent.mjs (generated into the fragment by authoring/tools/make-qa-fragment.mjs); measured 90-93% right on held-out player questions after one refine round (docs/harness-gaps/open-text.md); version 2 types on the iPhone keyboard (native text field)

name: Character judges your reply
summary: Each round a character says a line and the player picks one of 2-4 replies; the character rates it 0-100 into named bands ("cringe" to "W rizz") with a reaction line. Ratings and reactions are written by Muse at build time, so play is deterministic and replays.
when_to_use: Rizz and pickup-line simulators, convince-the-bouncer or the boss, a debate or roast judge, caption contests judged by a character, interview and negotiation games where a character scores what you say. The honest stand-in for "type anything and an AI judges it".
api: game provides nj_lines() (line per round), nj_options(), nj_ratings() (whole numbers 0-100 as strings), nj_reactions(), the last three flattened with `choices` entries per round; provides judge_line(), option_text(k), option_rating(k), band_label(r), state nj_points, last_rating, last_label, last_reaction, high_count, low_count, picked, locked; input nj_pick {index}; bind rounds round_done to line_done and lives hit to judged_low; art roles judge (a drawn character; real names as written, never photorealistic) and button; not with quiz, score or choice_story

params.labels: string, default "Cringe|Meh|Smooth|Legendary", the bands low to high split by |

gaps_it_closes: a character that judges what the player says, without an LLM at play time
notes: content comes from the npc_lines content step; a typed version (player writes the line) needs live_judge, which is a gap

name: Real map with a lit-up place
aliases: show the country on a map
country lit up on a map
summary: A geographically accurate map (world, a continent, a subregion or the US states) drawn from Natural Earth outlines, with one place filled in the accent colour and a pulsing ring at its label point so small countries still show.
when_to_use: Any game that shows a map: which-country-is-this quizzes, showing the country after an answer, a map behind a pin game, a Group's countries or states. Never ask the model to draw a map; write a `geo` section and use this.
api: manifest `geo` {pack: world|us_states, places: [names] or pick: {region, count, min_area, seed}, map: {x, y, w, h, view: world|fit|<continent>|<subregion>|[w,s,e,n]}}; game provides map_focus(): int (index into the geo places, -1 for none); the geo step provides geo_names(), geo_ids(), geo_capitals(), geo_continents(), geo_target() (list<vec2> lon/lat), geo_rings(), geo_ring_place(), geo_label() and the sprite `map`

params.x: float, set by the geo step
params.y: float, set by the geo step
params.w: float, set by the geo step
params.h: float, set by the geo step
params.ring: bool, default true: pulsing ring at the lit place

notes: Needs the manifest's `geo` section, which expander/geo.mjs turns into the map sprite, the geo_* functions and the rect and projection params. Example games pass the gate (authoring/content/geo/examples, built by tools/make-geo-games.mjs). Status building until the Studio pipeline calls applyGeo before expand and the bundle carries the packs and fragments (request in docs/harness-gaps/maps.md).

name: Map pin
summary: Tap the map to drop a pin; the great-circle distance to the answer in whole km sets the round's points (1000 falling to 0 at zero_km), a pin past far_km emits pin_far, and the pin, a line to the answer and the distance show before the next round.
when_to_use: Pin-the-city, where-in-the-world and closest-guess-wins geography games, with geo_map underneath. Bind rounds' round_done to pin_done and lives' hit to pin_far.
api: game provides map_target(): vec2 (vec(lon, lat), usually get_or(geo_target(), i, vec(0.0, 0.0))) and map_can_pin(): bool; provides state pin_at, pin_km, pin_shown, functions map_lonlat(p), map_screen(ll), pin_points(km), input map_tap {at: vec2}; the geo step sets x, y, w, h, ax, ay, kx, ky

params.grid: bool, default true: faint 30-degree grid dots
params.x, y, w, h, ax, ay, kx, ky: float, set by the geo step

gaps_it_closes: tap position to longitude and latitude
notes: Needs the manifest's `geo` section, which expander/geo.mjs turns into the map sprite, the geo_* functions and the rect and projection params. Example games pass the gate (authoring/content/geo/examples, built by tools/make-geo-games.mjs). Status building until the Studio pipeline calls applyGeo before expand and the bundle carries the packs and fragments (request in docs/harness-gaps/maps.md). Distance uses only arithmetic, sin, cos and sqrt (an asin series, no atan2 or pow), so replays match; the engine agrees with a JS great circle within 0.5 km in tools/test-geo.mjs.

name: Distance and direction on the globe
aliases: hot and cold on a map
summary: geo_km(a, b) great-circle km, geo_dir(a, b) 8-point compass direction and geo_closeness(a, b) 0–100 between two vec(lon, lat) points, deterministic in the engine.
when_to_use: Guess-the-country-by-name puzzles that answer with distance and direction, closest-guess scoring, and any rule that needs how far apart two places are.
api: provides geo_km(a: vec2, b: vec2): int, geo_dir(a, b): string, geo_closeness(a, b): int; points are vec(lon, lat), usually from geo_target()
gaps_it_closes: no trusted distance maths in rules
notes: Pure maths: works on today's engine with any vec(lon, lat) points. The coordinates themselves must come from the geo section (map_geometry), never from Muse.

name: Country or state outline
summary: One country's or US state's outline drawn big and alone, its main land mass fitted to a rect, from Natural Earth: guess the place from its shape.
when_to_use: Guess-the-country (or state) from its outline, silhouette dailies, and shape rounds in geography trivia.
api: manifest `geo` with `outline: {x, y, w, h}`; game provides outline_focus(): int; the geo step provides geo_outline(), geo_outline_place() and sets the rect

params.x, y, w, h: float, set by the geo step

notes: Needs the manifest's `geo` section, which expander/geo.mjs turns into the map sprite, the geo_* functions and the rect and projection params. Example games pass the gate (authoring/content/geo/examples, built by tools/make-geo-games.mjs). Status building until the Studio pipeline calls applyGeo before expand and the bundle carries the packs and fragments (request in docs/harness-gaps/maps.md).

name: Zoom-out picture
summary: A picture in a square window that starts zoomed in on a small crop and zooms out to the whole picture over a set time, driven by the game clock so replays match. The pictures are frames of the game's picture sprite, one per round.
when_to_use: Guess-the-picture games where seeing less is harder: wildlife close-ups, what is this object, zoomed-in characters or places. Pair with picture_quiz (choices) or typed_answer (type it). Pay more for early answers with zoom_left().
api: requires functions zoom_index(): int (which frame) and zoom_hold(): bool (show it whole, e.g. locked), event zoom_restart (bind to question_done); provides zoom_left(): int 100..0 by the clock, zoom_scale(): float; art role picture (frames, w and h 512 so it stays sharp). List it FIRST in uses: there is no clipping, so it masks around the window with $bg and later fragments draw on top

params.jitter: bool, default true (the crop point shifts per picture)

notes: masks with four $bg rects, so the backdrop is hidden around the window; an engine clip (image_clip) would remove that. Reaches the server with the next Studio bundle rebuild

name: Picture quiz
summary: The quiz fragment's rules (shuffled questions, shuffled choices, a timer per question, right and wrong events) with a layout that leaves the top of the screen for a picture: a short question line under it and the answers in a 2 x 2 grid.
when_to_use: Any multiple-choice round about a picture: zoom-out guessing, which animal, whose cartoon, what is this close-up, emoji or picture rebus with choices. Use quiz instead when there is no picture.
api: requires quiz_questions(), quiz_choices(), quiz_answers() like quiz; provides order, qi, opts, picked, locked, right_count, wrong_count, question_text(), correct_answer(); emits answered_right, answered_wrong, question_done. The picture goes in y 70..350 (zoom_reveal, or the game's own image node with frame get_or(order, qi, 0)). Conflicts with quiz
notes: derived from quiz.fragment.json; keep the rules in step if quiz changes

name: Spot the difference board
summary: Two pictures one above the other; tapping where they differ (in either picture) finds that difference and rings it in both, tapping anywhere else is a miss. The answer key is data written by the spot-difference generator, never guessed from pixels.
when_to_use: Spot-the-difference and find-what-changed games: chaotic group-chat screenshots, rooms, scenes, outfits. Build the pictures and the key with anomaly_generator (authoring/expander/spot-diff.mjs) from one scene.
api: requires functions diff_points(): list<ivec2>, diff_radii(): list<int>, diff_decoys(): list<ivec2> (written by spot-diff.mjs toAuthoring); art roles picture_a, picture_b; provides found, found_count, last_spot, spot_total(); emits spot_found, spot_missed, all_spots_found; wins when all are found (wins param). Bind score point to spot_found and lives hit to spot_missed
notes: the bot gate finds differences in about 3 s (it taps every object), so it flags too_short for one pair; people take 20-60 s. A gate profile for search games is requested from Bayan

name: Story quiz (a clip told in beats)
summary: A scripted clip cut into beats played in order: a quote card (speaker and line, optional picture per beat), a countdown and up to 4 Kahoot-coloured tiles, then a reveal panel with the real line and the punchline. Unranked by default: the score counts lines called.
when_to_use: Funny or story-first quizzes where the real answer is the joke or twist (a press conference that goes badly, a job interview gone wrong, a documentary narrated by a cat), and ordered step-by-step quizzes where each beat follows the last (proof steps, a recipe, a timeline). Not for shuffled trivia (quiz) or branching stories (choice_story).
api: game provides sq_speakers(), sq_lines(), sq_asks(), sq_choices() (choices per beat, flattened), sq_answers() (the real line, one of its choices) and sq_reveals(), all list<string> read from content; provides beat, called, picks (list<int>, the picked choice per beat in content order: put it in group_play.result.state), revealing, finished; inputs pick {index} and next; declare score {kind: points, ranked: false} for a story; params media (frames per beat, -1 none), tag (a PARODY label in the HUD), pace_label, hit_label, miss_label

params.time_ms: duration, default 15000, 0..60000 (countdown per beat; 0 for none; running out reveals with no pick)
params.media: string, default '', per-beat frame list like '0,1,-1'
params.sync_label: string, default 'In sync with the chaos:'
